image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) swimming in rippled blue water. The duck is captured from a side-rear angle, showing its iridescent green head, white neck ring, chest/brown breast, and greyish-brown body feathers. The bill is partially visible but mostly obscured by the angle and shadow. The legs and feet are completely submerged and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body plumage.

The folded wings along the side of the body appear broad and taper towards the tail, consistent with the anatomy of a duck.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear of the bird. While the specific 'curl' of the central feathers is subtle due to the angle and water interaction, the short tail structure is present.
